# Unversioned disposable prototype

Research fixture only; do not run these files against a hosted database. The caller-settable `forms.pilot_fixture` marker is an accident guard, not a security boundary. No real approval row or real identity is included. The synthetic HTTP script accepts only a disposable loopback endpoint and uses a public test JWT key.

The SQL replaces existing function bodies and preserves their existing ACLs, introduces an empty owner/site gate, and locks the gate and website during guarded operations. It explicitly revokes service-role access and rejects inherited table or column privileges. The caller-settable fixture marker is not authorization; only the synthetic table owner can administer approvals in this experiment, and any real operator identity needs separate design. Rollback first revokes service acceptance, origin lookup and host completion and checks effective denial, then restores the local source bodies and eight held ACLs. Neither file is a production migration or hosted rollback: target identities, dependencies, inherited privileges, runner atomicity, rollout and unknown outcomes require separate review. Revocation denies even existing same-ID retries until approval returns; responses and idempotency data remain intact. Public owner reads remain governed by their existing RLS and are not pilot-filtered.

The table privilege check includes PostgreSQL 17 `MAINTAIN`, including roles reachable through `SET ROLE` without inherited privileges. The rollback is a fail-closed disable, not a restoration of the previous service grants; any re-enable requires a separately reviewed procedure. The PG17 HTTP fixture substitutes synthetic `auth.jwt()` and `auth.uid()` helpers to read test claims, so it does not verify the deployed authentication or claim configuration.

After removal, an ambiguous submission cannot be resolved by ordinary retry until reapproval; a denied retry must not be presented as proof that it was never received. Owner status changes, recipient disable/retry and response deletion are also denied by the gate, while existing owner RLS reads remain as before. A production design needs a separately authorized, bounded reconciliation and emergency cleanup path before adopting this behavior; this fixture does not provide one. The begin RPC takes the existing account-row lock before the site gate to avoid reversing account-deletion lock order, but other races and deadlocks still require tests.

For local PGlite run `node --test supabase/tests/forms-pilot-scope.test.mjs`. The PostgREST fixture requires a freshly initialized disposable PostgreSQL and PostgREST with roles and HTP migrations 000–009 and quota 28, the eight held ACLs, the prototype and `seed.sql` (both set the local fixture marker in their SQL session). Configure PostgREST with the synthetic key in `postgrest-check.mjs`. `PILOT_FIXTURE=disposable PILOT_FIXTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ node supabase/tests/fixtures/forms-pilot-scope/postgrest-check.mjs` checks held access; after a disposable regrant of begin/challenge/save/status only, set `PILOT_FIXTURE_PHASE=open` to check owner/site isolation and retry. These checks do not prove hosted behavior.
